questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Harder to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: What is a bobtail?

options.text: A tractor that goes faster than the speed limit
A tractor that goes slower than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires near the back of the brakes.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to have the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Have the same chance of rolling over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can make your trailer skid.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. Always make sure there is enough space in traffic to safely enter or cross.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies service lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes when connecting glad hands. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator to the floor.

questions.explanation: To avoid tipping over with a trailer, steer gently and smoothly. Do not make sudden movements.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Triple combination trailers are most likely to have the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside the trailer
Placed as low as possible inside the trailer
Placed on the passenger side of the trailer
Placed on the driver's side of the trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside the trailer
questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low as possible to reduce rollover risk. Do not place weight mainly on one side of the trailer, as this makes the trailer lean and increases rollover risk.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes
The front and rear wheels will move in different paths
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels will move in different paths
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Trailers make this effect more pronounced.

questions.question: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for escaping air
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from the rear valves, the entire vehicle is receiving air.

questions.question: When connecting glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often:
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, match the colors together. Color coding helps drivers avoid mistakes. Service lines are often blue and emergency lines are often red.

questions.question: A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open
The rear trailer to detach from the combination

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual
Push the brake pedal as you normally would
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), apply the brakes the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: If the trailer begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel one way, then the other

questions.explanation: If your trailer begins to skid, release the brakes to help the wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels have traction, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.
